# /world

The root computer's description of the world. The desktop page's network
fabric (other/net/fabric.js) runs exactly what is here; edit, then
`worldctl apply` (or reload) to rebuild it.

- `net/segments.yaml` — network segments (LANs, `internet`) and latency in ms
- `net/routers/<id>.yaml` — JS routers: interfaces, routes, NAT, port forwards, DHCP, DNS forwarding, firewall
- `boxes/<id>.yaml` — machines: image, hostname, interfaces (static `a.b.c.d/nn` or `dhcp`), extra users and files.
  `local` is the player's own machine (the page itself).
- `images/<name>/image.yaml` + `rootfs/` — what a new box is provisioned with (`from:` inherits another image)
- `state/` — DHCP leases and other runtime state the fabric saves

Files seeded from the repo are kept up to date until you edit them; edited
files are yours. Put world-specific networks, servers and users here (or in a
world pack), never in host JS.

# TrustRoot's ACME server: free, automated 90-day certificates for any domain you control.
image: acme
hostname: acme.trustroot.net
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: internet, addr: 23.51.7.20/32, onlink: true }
dns: [8.8.8.8]

# The player's own machine (runs on the desktop page itself).
hostname: tehboxen
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: home, addr: dhcp }

# Authoritative registry for every public zone (the world's root/TLD servers in one box).
image: dns-registry
hostname: ns.registry.net
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: internet, addr: 198.41.0.4/32, onlink: true }
dns: [127.0.0.1]

# Public recursive resolver.
image: dns-resolver
hostname: resolver1.public-dns.net
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: internet, addr: 8.8.8.8/32, onlink: true }
dns: [127.0.0.1]

# Public recursive resolver.
image: dns-resolver
hostname: resolver2.public-dns.net
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: internet, addr: 1.1.1.1/32, onlink: true }
dns: [127.0.0.1]

# Public recursive resolver.
image: dns-resolver
hostname: resolver3.public-dns.net
interfaces:
  - { name: eth0, segment: internet, addr: 9.9.9.9/32, onlink: true }
dns: [127.0.0.1]

# TrustRoot's ACME server (RFC 8555, http-01): issues 90-day certificates from the R1 CA.
from: base
version: 1
packages: [nodejs]
world_files:
  /etc/acmed/issuer.key: pki/private/trustroot-r1.key
  /etc/acmed/issuer.pem: pki/issuers/trustroot-r1.pem
modes:
  /usr/sbin/acmed: "755"
  /etc/rc.d/acmed: "755"
  /etc/acmed/issuer.key: "600"
  /etc/acmed/issuer.pem: "644"

{
  "listen": 80,
  "base": "http://acme.trustroot.net",
  "issuer": "/etc/acmed/issuer.pem",
  "issuerKey": "/etc/acmed/issuer.key",
  "days": 90,
  "state": "/var/lib/acmed",
  "tos": "http://acme.trustroot.net/terms"
}

#!/bin/sh
# acmed: TrustRoot's ACME directory on :80 (/etc/acmed.json).
mkdir -p /var/lib/acmed
node /usr/sbin/acmed /etc/acmed.json >> /var/log/acmed.log 2>&1 &

# Minimal server: root, /etc/rc running /etc/rc.d/* at boot.
version: 1
packages: []
users:
  - { name: root, uid: 0, gid: 0, home: /root, shell: /bin/sh }
modes:
  /etc/rc: "755"

The programs included with this system are free software.
Unauthorized access to this system is prohibited.

#!/bin/sh
# Run by the kernel at boot, as root: starts every executable in /etc/rc.d.
for s in /etc/rc.d/*; do
  if [ -x "$s" ]; then
    "$s" start
  fi
done

# DNS server: the interim node `named` (until dnsmasq is ported).
from: base
version: 1
packages: [nodejs]
modes:
  /usr/sbin/named: "755"
  /etc/rc.d/named: "755"

# Authoritative for every zone in /etc/named/zones (BIND zone files, origin = file name).
from: dns
version: 1

$ORIGIN public-dns.net.
$TTL 3600
@         IN SOA ns.registry.net. hostmaster.registry.net. 1 7200 3600 1209600 300
@         IN NS  ns.registry.net.
resolver1 IN A   8.8.8.8
resolver2 IN A   1.1.1.1
resolver3 IN A   9.9.9.9

$ORIGIN registry.net.
$TTL 3600
@         IN SOA ns.registry.net. hostmaster.registry.net. 1 7200 3600 1209600 300
@         IN NS  ns.registry.net.
ns        IN A   198.41.0.4

$ORIGIN trustroot.net.
$TTL 3600
@         IN SOA ns.registry.net. hostmaster.registry.net. 1 7200 3600 1209600 300
@         IN NS  ns.registry.net.
@         IN A   23.51.7.20
acme      IN A   23.51.7.20
{ "listen": "0.0.0.0", "zones": "/etc/named/zones", "recursion": false }

# Recursive resolver: answers from cache, asks the registry for the rest.
from: dns
version: 1
{ "listen": "0.0.0.0", "zones": "/etc/named/zones", "recursion": true, "forwarders": ["198.41.0.4"] }

# The player's home router: NAT to the Internet, DHCP and a DNS forwarder on the LAN.
hostname: home-router
interfaces:
  - { name: wan, segment: internet, addr: 73.42.18.9/32 }
  - { name: lan, segment: home, addr: 192.168.1.1/24 }
routes:
  - { to: default, dev: wan }
masquerade: [wan]
forwards: []
dhcp:
  iface: lan
  range: 192.168.1.100-192.168.1.199
  dns: [192.168.1.1]
  domain: lan
  lease: 86400
dns:
  listen: lan
  forwarders: [8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1]

# Network segments: every interface plugs into one. Latency is one-way, in ms.
internet:
  latency: 12
home:
  latency: 0

#!/bin/sh
# World automation: the root computer runs this as godshand at every boot, after the base
# system (openssl, busybox…) is installed. Each /world/rc.d/* script must be idempotent.
for s in /world/rc.d/*; do
  if [ -x "$s" ]; then
    "$s"
  fi
done

#!/bin/sh
# TrustRoot, the world's public CA: a root (in every box's trust bundle, from /world/pki/trust)
# and the R1 issuing CA its ACME server (box acme, acme.trustroot.net) signs certificates with.
# Made once; delete /world/pki to start the world's PKI over (then reprovision the acme box).
P=/world/pki
if [ -f $P/trust/trustroot-root.pem ] && [ -f $P/issuers/trustroot-r1.pem ]; then
  exit 0
fi
mkdir -p $P/trust $P/issuers $P/private
chmod 700 $P/private
cat > $P/private/ext.cnf <<'EXT'
[root]
basicConstraints=critical,CA:true
keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign
subjectKeyIdentifier=hash
[issuer]
basicConstraints=critical,CA:true,pathlen:0
keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign,digitalSignature
extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth,clientAuth
subjectKeyIdentifier=hash
authorityKeyIdentifier=keyid
EXT
openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-384 -nodes \
  -keyout $P/private/trustroot-root.key -out $P/trust/trustroot-root.pem \
  -subj "/C=US/O=TrustRoot Inc./CN=TrustRoot Global Root CA" -days 7300 \
  -config $P/private/ext.cnf -extensions root
openssl req -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -nodes \
  -keyout $P/private/trustroot-r1.key -out $P/private/trustroot-r1.csr \
  -subj "/C=US/O=TrustRoot Inc./CN=TrustRoot R1"
openssl x509 -req -in $P/private/trustroot-r1.csr -CA $P/trust/trustroot-root.pem \
  -CAkey $P/private/trustroot-root.key -set_serial 0x$(openssl rand -hex 8) -days 3650 \
  -extfile $P/private/ext.cnf -extensions issuer -out $P/issuers/trustroot-r1.pem
chmod 600 $P/private/*.key
chmod 644 $P/trust/trustroot-root.pem $P/issuers/trustroot-r1.pem
echo "pki: TrustRoot root + R1 issuer created"
